svg.text: Why the ugly waveform is the right one

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: De-emphasis is pre-distortion, not amplification. A transmitter cannot boost high frequencies without spending peak amplitude, so

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: it lowers the low-frequency content instead and lets the channel's own loss restore the shape. The eye at the receiver is the

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: point; the waveform at the driver is deliberately ugly.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The cost is that the launched eye is smaller than the swing would allow. A three-tap FFE that de-emphasises by 6 dB gives away 6 dB

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: of launch amplitude to buy back more than that at the far end -- which is a good trade only on a channel that actually has the

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
